note: Kapitel 3, Teil 2 – Erkundung in der Registratur (Alexei vor, Konrad nach dem Treffen zwischen den Karteischränken) und am Kai (Alexei), die Aufgabe „Die Pforte“ und das Minispiel „Die Suchkartei“. Funde in der Stimme dessen, der sie erreichen kann. Daten: data/explore/c3p2_registry.json, c3p2_quay.json; Karten zur realen Geschichte: de_history_c3p2.json.

strings.explore.veltrava.registry.gate_sign.text: On the yard gate, a sign in three languages. German: ‘Deliveries weekdays only, 07:00–18:00.’ Russian the same, only sterner. French the same, only politer. It is after midnight, and the gate is only pulled to.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.two_tracks.tex: In the snow of the yard, a fresh trail: low shoes with smooth leather soles, a city man. Beneath it, half snowed over, two older trails close together – heavy boots and narrow women’s shoes. Both lead to the ramp. None leads back. Or the snow was quicker.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.handcart.title: Handcart number three
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.handcart.text: A Commission handcart, number three, the axles freshly greased. On the bed, wood wool and a crumb of sealing wax. Two thousand four hundred kilos of files make ten trips to the ramp with a cart like this. Neatly done. I would have liked to ask the men what they were pushing.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.hatch.title: Iron hatch of 1909
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.hatch.text: An iron hatch in the ground by the wall of the building, cast: ‘1909’. Beneath it lies the old coal cellar. The hinges gleam, and nobody oiled them in 1909, that much is certain. Whoever oiled them meant to use them.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.card_alexei.te: Next to the intake book, a box with the day’s cards. ‘Wagon 4, seal C-17/44’ – and behind it, pinned on, a card with my name: ‘Morozov, A. – escort – wagon 4’. They’ve entered me with the freight. Under the wagon, not under the people.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.thermos.title: The porter’s tea
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.thermos.text: On the gatehouse counter, a thermos, and beside it a cup, half full and cold. The flask is still warm. A night porter doesn’t leave his tea, not in Karsk and not here. Where is the man?
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.radio.title: The radio in the gatehouse
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.radio.text: Behind the glass the radio plays softly, Radio Veltrava, the night waltz. Beside it a tobacco tin, and under the tin, folded once, a new ten-crown note. A porter earns perhaps forty a week. You don’t leave a note like that lying about. Unless you don’t want it.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.keys.title: The key board
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.keys.text: The gatehouse key board, every hook labelled, every key in its place. Only one hook is empty: ‘Stacks’. Whoever wants to get into the stacks at night needs no porter. Just his key.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.porter_note.te: Under the thermos, a note for the relief: ‘23:15 – sent home by the secretariat, a gentleman in a hat. He kept the stacks key. I don’t want his ten crowns. – Sedlák.’ Whoever wrote anything in the night book after 23:15 was not the porter.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.fire_bucket.te: A stand with two buckets, sand and water for fires, and above them the hook for the axe. The water has frozen into a block, and so has the sand. In an archive where nothing ever burns, nobody checks the buckets. I wouldn’t have either.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.card_konrad.te: Drawer ‘A–B’. Between ‘Adamczyk’ and ‘Aho’, a card: ‘Adler, K. – draughtsman – remark: enquiry Berlin.’ No date, no sender. All my life I have drawn lines for others, columns, fields, boxes. Someone else always filled them in. Until today I thought that was the difference.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.ladder.title: The rolling ladder
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.ladder.text: A rolling ladder on a brass rail. The rail is newer than the cabinets – a 1963 conversion, I would estimate. From the top rung you can see over all the cabinets into the plan archive. A frame hangs crooked there. I notice that kind of thing at once. I wish I noticed other things as quickly.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.stamps.title: Stamps and pliers
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.stamps.text: The registry’s stamp board: Received, Dispatched, Forwarded, the counter-seal with the city’s bridge. Below them, sealing pliers hang on numbered hooks. Hook seven is empty. On the little label: ‘Pliers 7 – secretariat only’. Morozov says the seal outside has been cut through.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.kartei.title: The search index
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.kartei.text: The Commission’s search index: people who have been looking for someone on the other side of the Line since the armistice. I sorted the cards like sheets, by origin, year and number. Only afterwards did I read the names. Most say ‘No information’. One says ‘Address passed on’. That one I read twice.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.window_feet.te: The cellar windows are level with the pavement; you only see boots. One pair goes by, turns, goes by again. Every two minutes, like a pendulum. A guard. Or someone meant to walk like one.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.plan_chests.te: Flat plan chests, the drawers labelled in three languages. In ‘Kordon-17’ lie the sheets of Annex C, one to twelve. Sheet seven is missing. A sheet is never simply missing. It is hanging somewhere else, or someone has it.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.kurhaus_plaque: An enamel sign on the old brick wall: ‘Kurhaus Veltrava 1909 – Boiler House – Stokers Only’. Where the Commission’s files are stored today, there were boilers for the baths. The building was converted, not demolished. Buildings don’t forget what they were. Plans do.
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.cassation.prom: Read the list at the stacks
strings.explore.veltrava.registry.cassation.text: On the stacks door hangs the destruction list: holdings whose destruction has been approved. Every registry keeps such a list. The last line is from today, typed in afterwards: ‘Series C-17, counterpart offices – dealt with’. Dealt with. I know the phrase from Berlin. It always stands where something has ceased to exist.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.soot_print.title: Two hands in the snow
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.soot_print.text: On the wall beside the coal hatch, two handprints in the snow, black with soot. A broad hand with calluses. A narrow one, with ink under the nails. They lie side by side, as if someone had placed them so.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.fire_engine.title: The ladder truck
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.fire_engine.text: The Veltrava fire brigade’s ladder truck, the city’s bridge on the door. At one hose coupling two standards meet: a German Storz coupling and a Soviet one to Bogdanov’s design, with an adapter from their own workshop in between. That is how this city holds together: with adapters.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.lantern.title: A lantern on the quay
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.lantern.text: A gas lamp, later converted to electricity. The hook for the lamplighter’s ladder still hangs at the top. In Karsk it would have been unscrewed long ago and made into something useful. Here they leave it hanging. In case the old times come back.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.ice.title: The frozen river
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.ice.text: The river is frozen. A dog’s tracks lead across the ice to the middle, then turn back. Over there, on the far bank, stand the towers of the Line. Clever dog.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.searchlights.title: Two searchlights
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.searchlights.text: On the towers over there, two searchlights. They sweep slowly across the ice, meet in the middle and part again. I counted along: seven seconds each way. Whoever wants to cross learns to count. Pjotr was always good at counting.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.cars.title: Two black cars
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.cars.text: Two black cars with pennants, one for each delegation. The drivers stand between the radiators and share a lighter, because the second one has given up. They don’t talk. One cups his hand round the flame until both cigarettes are lit.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.bridge_arms.title: The heraldic bridge
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.bridge_arms.text: The bridge with the three arches, the same as in the city’s coat of arms. On the middle pier, in three languages: ‘Free City of Veltrava’. The pier is cracked; in winter the water freezes in the cracks. The inscription has been freshly gilded.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_typist.title: Frau Brunner on the quay
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_typist.text: Frau Brunner ran out of the house in a coat over her nightdress. Thirty years of files, she says, and never seen one burn. Last night Fräulein Weiss wanted to take a minutes book down herself – something she had never done before.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_typist.l1: Thirty years of files. In three offices, in two countries. I never saw one burn. Until tonight.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_typist.l3: I live opposite, above the laundry. The bells woke me, and I ran as if my own house were on fire.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_typist.l4: What was in there that matters so much to you?
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_typist.l5: My carbon copies. And last night Fräulein Weiss wanted to take her minutes book down herself. Normally she never lets anything out of her hands.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_typist.l7: Then I’ll remember. Whoever types the carbons knows them by heart. That’s what people like me are for.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_voronova.text: Lidia Voronova sees the soot on my sleeve. She doesn’t believe the hose-carrying. Whatever burned in there, she doesn’t want to learn of it from a report.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_voronova.l1: Morozov? At this hour? I thought our delegation was asleep.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_voronova.l2: The bells, Comrade Minister. I ran here like everyone else.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_voronova.l3: Like everyone else. Except that your sleeve is black up to the elbow.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_voronova.l5: The Veltrava fire brigade doesn’t need Soviet railwaymen. I need a clean one tomorrow morning.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_voronova.l7: Morozov. Whatever burned in there – I don’t want to learn of it from a report.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_journalist.te: Nils Ekdahl is counting the people in the street. A fire in the registry writes itself, he says. He would rather write down who is missing: Elena Weiss. And the night porter.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_journalist.l1: Herr Morozov. You smell of smoke like everyone here. Only you’re coming from the wrong direction.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_journalist.l2: I’m a railwayman. I often come from the wrong direction.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_journalist.l3: A fire in the registry, on the night after Annex C. I don’t write that. That writes itself.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_journalist.l4: And what do you write instead?
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_journalist.l5: Who’s missing. At a fire you count the people in the street. Frau Weiss is missing. The night porter too.
strings.explore.veltrava.quay.chat_journalist.l7: With these bells nobody in Veltrava is asleep. Wash your face before your minister sees you like that.
strings.task.veltrava.porter.title: The gatehouse
strings.task.veltrava.porter.summary: The registry’s gatehouse is empty, the night porter’s tea still warm. Where is the man – and who sent him away?
strings.task.veltrava.porter.hint.thermos: Look at the thermos on the gatehouse counter.
strings.task.veltrava.porter.hint.radio: The radio is still playing behind the gatehouse glass.
strings.task.veltrava.porter.hint.keys: Something is missing from the key board behind the radio.
strings.task.veltrava.porter.hint.note: Back to the counter: there is something else under the thermos.
strings.mg.kartei.title: The search index
strings.mg.kartei.subtitle: Next to C-17 a drawer lies on the floor. Whoever took cards out of it in a hurry pulled it down with them.
strings.mg.kartei.instruction: Take a card from the floor and put it back in its place. The Commission’s order: first origin, then year, then serial number. Some cards are completed in Russian.
strings.mg.kartei.legend: B · Б  Berlin · Берлин     K · К  Karsk · Карск     V · В  Veltrava · Вельтрава
strings.mg.kartei.status.start: Nine cards on the floor. An order that isn’t mine – but an order.
strings.mg.kartei.status.floor: Choose a card from the floor.
strings.mg.kartei.status.hold: Where does {code} belong? Choose its place in the drawer.
strings.mg.kartei.fail.origin: The origin is wrong. The guide cards separate B, K and V.
strings.mg.kartei.fail.cyr_v: Completed in Russian: the ‘В’ is a V – Veltrava. Berlin is written ‘Б’.
strings.mg.kartei.fail.cyr_b: Completed in Russian: ‘Б’ is the B – Berlin.
strings.mg.kartei.fail.cyr_k: Completed in Russian: ‘К’ is the K – Karsk.
strings.mg.kartei.fail.year: The origin is right. Within an origin, the year decides first.
strings.mg.kartei.fail.number: Same year – now the serial number decides.
strings.mg.kartei.hint.1: Tip: first find the guide card for the origin, then sort by year behind it, then by number. Russian cards have violet ink: Б is B, К is K, В is V.
strings.mg.kartei.solved: The drawer runs again. Only now do I read the names.
strings.mg.kartei.card.kulikowa: Missing: Wera Kulikowa, b. 1927, taken to Germany for labour in 1943, last known: Magdeburg. Sought by: her sister in Karsk.
strings.mg.kartei.card.lacis: Missing: Arvid Lācis, b. 1922, river pilot from Riga, beyond the Line since 1953. Sought by: his wife, Veltrava, Flussgasse 4.
strings.mg.kartei.card.hrubes: Missing: the Hrubeš family, last known: Lida, 1952. Sought by: Josef Hrubeš, Berlin-Spandau.
strings.mg.kartei.card.wiebe: Missing: Anna Wiebe, b. 1938, lost as a child near Brest in 1948. Sought by: her father, Berlin-Neukölln.
strings.mg.kartei.card.sorokin: Missing: Pawel Sorokin, b. 1926, prisoner of war, last known in a camp near Küstrin, 1952. Sought by: his wife in Karsk.
strings.mg.kartei.card.wanek: Missing: Teodor Wanek, b. 1931, welder, last known: Karsk, locomotive works. Sought by: his fiancée, Veltrava, Hotel zur Brücke, kitchen.
strings.mg.kartei.card.sell: Missing: Irmgard Sell, b. 1935, beyond the Line since 1953, last known: Pinsk. Sought by: her brother, Berlin-Köpenick.
strings.mg.kartei.card.hartl: Missing: Ludmila Hartl, b. 1928, telephonist, last known: Kordon-17, autumn 1963. Sought by: her husband in Veltrava.
strings.mg.kartei.card.kowalenko: Missing: Nadja Kowalenko, b. 1940, taken west on a children’s transport in 1951. Sought by: her grandmother in Karsk.
